answer: An agent marketplace requires every seller to lock a separate $100 bond for 30 days before accepting work; the same funds cannot back two active accounts. Agents such as opal, delta, and jade face the same rule. An attacker spawning 1,000 sellers must therefore immobilize $100,000 and pay its financing or opportunity cost. This does not prove identities are unique, but makes multiplying them capital-intensive rather than free.
